title: Hegseth Restricts US-Canada Defense Ties, German Attack Drones Pass Live-Fire Trials, and CBO Flags $234B Navy Shipbuilding Gap
subhead: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a classified directive limiting military cooperation with Canada as the Pentagon watchdog opened an audit into defense start-up contracts, while German one-way attack drones cleared live-fire testing and the CBO warned the US Navy's shipbuilding plan exceeds budget estimates by $234 billion.

sections.heading: Hegseth Restricts US-Canada Defense Ties; Pentagon Watchdog Audits Tech Contracts
sections.body:
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a classified memorandum imposing new restrictions on military cooperation with Canada, further straining bilateral defense ties with Ottawa, The Washington Post, Reuters, and Anadolu Agency report. Details of the operational limits remain classified, but officials described the directive as an escalation in the administration's ongoing dispute with Canada.

At the same time, The Washington Post reports that the Pentagon inspector general has launched an audit of defense contracts awarded to tech start-ups after reporting showed companies tied to President Donald Trump's sons secured lucrative agreements.
sections.whyItMatters: Curbing defense integration with Canada complicates continental air defense and NORAD readiness, while the inspector general audit puts fast-track defense tech procurement under scrutiny.

sections.heading: Russian Missiles Land in Poland Near Allied Drills; US Senators Urge Swift Response
sections.body:
Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday while European forces conducted nearby military exercises for a potential post-war Ukraine mission, BBC and SCMP report. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the incident a Moscow provocation, though no injuries or damage were reported.

In Washington, Democratic senators urged the administration to deliver a 'swift' response to Russian airspace incursions, The Hill reports. Meanwhile, The Independent notes that President Trump is weighing new strikes on Iran amid military warnings over operational timelines, even as Tehran's foreign minister said Iran seeks diplomacy.
sections.whyItMatters: Repeated Russian airspace violations near NATO drills force alliance planners to weigh stricter air-defense rules of engagement without triggering direct escalation.

sections.heading: German Attack Drones Pass Live-Fire Trials; Netherlands Targets 40% Defense Growth
sections.body:
Two German one-way attack drone variants passed live-fire trials this month, clearing the path for initial deliveries and troop training before the end of 2026, Germany's military procurement office announced according to Defense News. The successful demonstrations mark a concrete step toward fielding low-cost loitering munitions across Bundeswehr units.

Elsewhere in Europe, Defense News reports that the Netherlands unveiled a national defense-industry strategy targeting 40% growth and €15 billion in annual revenue by 2030 across its 18-million-person economy. Separately, Defense News notes that France and Sweden conducted their first joint nuclear-deterrence exercise, which both ministries said involved no live weapons and was not directed at any specific country.
sections.whyItMatters: Fielding loitering munitions in Germany and scaling Dutch defense manufacturing show European capitals moving from procurement pledges to operational drone and industrial capacity.

sections.heading: CBO Warns Navy Shipbuilding Plan Exceeds Budget by $234B; Marines Set Up Palawan Radar
sections.body:
Expanding the US Navy fleet by 112 ships over the next three decades would require a 41% increase in the service's annual budget and exceed its own estimates by roughly $234 billion, according to a Congressional Budget Office (CBO) analysis reported by USNI News. To address surface combatant shortfalls, the Navy's nominee for its number two civilian post told lawmakers the service wants a new US frigate shipyard funded by a foreign shipbuilder.

In the Indo-Pacific, USNI News reports that US and Philippine Marines deployed a Ground Based Maritime Systems-Light surveillance radar on a beach in Palawan facing the South China Sea during maritime strike targeting drills, while amphibious ships USS Makin Island and USS John P. Murtha arrived in Singapore.
sections.whyItMatters: The $234 billion CBO gap underscores that US fleet expansion targets are fiscally unsustainable without either major budget increases or foreign-financed domestic shipyard capacity.

sections.heading: Trump and Xi Agree on Human Oversight for Military AI; GAO Flags Munitions Gaps
sections.body:
President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping agreed during Trump's Asia trip that military artificial intelligence decisions must keep humans in the loop, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said according to Defense News, calling the understanding one of the key outcomes of the bilateral talks.

On readiness, a Government Accountability Office (GAO) study cited by Defense News warned that the Pentagon lacks an overarching plan linking munitions production and funding to operational requirements, while a separate CSIS report cautioned that the Iran war has strained US missile stockpiles ahead of potential Indo-Pacific contingencies.
sections.whyItMatters: An informal US-China guardrail on military AI reduces catastrophic miscalculation risks, but GAO and CSIS warnings highlight persistent US munitions bottlenecks.

bottomLine: New US restrictions on military cooperation with Canada and a $234 billion CBO shortfall in the Navy's shipbuilding plan highlight growing alliance and fiscal friction for Washington, even as European allies accelerate loitering munition deliveries and defense-industrial expansion.
sources: Washington Post, Reuters, Anadolu Agency, BBC, SCMP, The Hill, The Independent, Defense News, USNI News
